correctness.rationale: For any measurable B of area t in the unit square, mixed Hölder including endpoints gives exact rank-one norm ||P_B||=||1_B||_{p,q}||1_B||_{p′,q′}/t. With m(x) vertical section length, s=measure{m>0}, h=ess sup m, the six endpoint expressions reduce to concave moments ∫m^a or convex moments ∫m^r and products of h and s. Jensen and m^r≤m yield K=t^{-|1/p−1/q|}, with sharp two-height spike/dust sequences. Strict Jensen or m^r equality forbids attainment at each of the eight non-corner boundary pairs; all equal-exponent corners give 1, opposite corners attain iff s=h=1. If near-extremal then both factors tend to 1: strict concavity enforces m→t in L1 with h→1, or convex moment equality enforces s→1 and ∫m(1−m)→0; converses follow by continuity. Independent numeric endpoint check on five pairs confirmed bounds and opposite-corner equality. Finite grids are not used for arbitrary measurable functions.

value.rationale: A uniform boundedness phenomenon in mixed-Lebesgue averaging has a sharp endpoint fixed-measure quantitative form with different geometry from interior exponents. A complete all-area norm/attainment/rigidity classification at the nonreflexive boundaries is useful for projection geometry and mixed-norm operator stability, especially the spike-versus-dust dichotomy.

limitations: Only single-set rank-one averaging operators and nonreflexive pairs on unit product Lebesgue square, not interior exponents nor general conditional expectations.
Supremum is nonattained at eight noncorner endpoint pairs despite exact formula.
